newsitem.title: GERMANY: German unions consolidate further, IG Metall grows.
newsitem.headline: German unions consolidate further, IG Metall grows.

text.p: A further reduction in the number of independent trade unions in Germany was likely on Thursday as Germany's giant IG Metall union said it was merging with the smaller GHK wood and synthetics trade union.

IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel told a news briefing during the German Federation of Trade unions (DGB) congress in Dresden that the 160,000 members of the GHK union would join its some 2.75 million members as part of the same body from 1999.
The metal and engineering union, already Germany's largest trade union, has already agreed with the GTB textiles and clothing union to take on its 200,000 members.

"This brings together a trade union which by the next millenium will have more than three million members," Zwickel said, adding that the aim of the merger was to create a "powerful and forceful" organisation.

Together with the planned merger of the HBV banking union with unions representing postal, media and printing sector workers, and a similar fusion of chemical and mining unions, the new move would bring the number of separate trade unions in Germany down from the current 15 to nine.

While both IG Metall and GHK said the merger was not primarily motivated by cost-savings, Zwickel acknowledged the move would "reduce costs both in the administrative and technical areas" of the unions' operations.
GHK chairman said the current finances of the wood and synthetics union could if needed fund a long-term strike but that it was "thinking ahead".

He added that IG Metall and GHK were also ideologically compatible in their support for a 35-hour working week and willingness to fight for full sick pay entitlements, currently threatened by a new federal law.
German trade unions have in recent years seen a decline in membership numbers to something over nine million out of a total workforce of over 30 million.
